Platforms that vanish a moment after you land on them, forcing you to keep moving up
Trusses, ladders and wall scrambles between the platform sections
A small start area at the foot of the tower where players pick their avatar before setting off
The payoff platform at the top of the tower
Two boxes standing side by side at the base of the tower, each showing the avatar outfit it gives you

layout_placement.text: The reward area at the top of the tower, reached by finishing the climb
Two touch volumes, one on each box, applying that box's avatar to the player for the duration of the run

mechanics: Choosing a box gives you that avatar temporarily
notes: The two avatar boxes have no option ID. They are carried as free text in both lists — drawn as boxes, placed as two trigger volumes — so nothing is lost, but they route nothing.
social-hub bent from 'start hub and shop' to the avatar-selection area at the tower's foot; it is the same geometry doing a different job.
course-tower carries P2 as well as the genre's P6, because a spiral ascent overhangs itself.

open_questions.ask: How should the tower look — bright neon like a classic Tower of Hell, stone and torches, or plain coloured blocks?
What are the two boxes offering — two set outfits, two morphs like an animal or a robot, or two gear loadouts?
Do you want checkpoints up the tower, or is falling back to the bottom part of the point?

enriched_invented.detail: a neutral sky or minimal backdrop behind the tower
the selection area sitting in the foreground with the tower rising behind it
simple challenges rather than any specific obstacle type

notes_for_us: A two-way choice pedestal is a common Roblox pattern — pick a morph, pick a weapon, pick a team — and there is no option for it. social-hub covers the area around it but not the choice itself, so the boxes ship as free text and the count of two survives only because count exists.

Nothing in the prompt says how the tower should look, and Tower Obby's reference has a strong visual identity that it would be easy to inherit without being asked. Left theme null rather than importing it.

unmatched_options.text: two box options at the base, and you wear the one you choose temporarily
the chosen avatar is worn only temporarily

skill_gap.name: no choice pedestal option
skill_gap.why: picking one of N options off physical plinths at the start of a course is a standard Roblox pattern with no ID; it is geometry plus a trigger and had to be written twice as free text
